title: Post Office vs FD vs Arbitrage Fund: Optimising Post-Tax Returns
description: Post Office deposits and Bank FDs offer fixed, guaranteed returns but are fully taxable at your income tax slab rate. Arbitrage funds aim for market-linked re.

faq.q: What is the main advantage of an arbitrage fund over an FD for a high-income earner?
faq.a: The main advantage is tax efficiency. Arbitrage funds held for over a year are taxed as Long-Term Capital Gains at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh, while FD interest is fully taxed at your income slab rate, which can be as high as 30%.

faq.q: Are Post Office deposits completely risk-free?
faq.a: Yes, Post Office deposits carry a sovereign guarantee from the Government of India, making them one of the safest investment options in terms of capital safety.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from an FD or Post Office Time Deposit before maturity?
faq.a: Yes, both FDs and Post Office Time Deposits generally allow premature withdrawal, but it usually comes with a penalty, such as a reduction in the interest rate. NSCs have stricter lock-in periods.

faq.q: How are arbitrage fund returns generated?
faq.a: Arbitrage funds generate returns by simultaneously buying a stock in the cash market and selling its futures contract in the derivatives market, or vice-versa, to profit from the temporary price difference.

faq.q: Is there any deposit insurance for Bank FDs?
faq.a: Yes, deposits in commercial banks are insured by the DICGC up to ₹5 lakhs (principal and interest combined) per bank, per depositor, providing a safety net.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment period for an arbitrage fund to get tax benefits?
faq.a: To avail of the favourable Long-Term Capital Gains tax treatment, units of an arbitrage fund must be held for more than one year.
